_changelog: Initial goldens, Task R3 (deterministic CPU rasterizer, first solid-shading + wireframe + overlay pass). REGENERATED at Task R6 (S7a): materials/lighting/sky/analytic-ground landed -- see _regeneration_note below for why all three hashes legitimately moved. Task R7 (S7a, sun shadow map + ruling SR-21's overlay depth-fix): INVESTIGATED, NOT regenerated -- all three hashes are BYTE-IDENTICAL to R6's, verified directly (RasterGolden.* all pass unchanged against these exact committed sha256 values, in both Release and Debug). This is not an oversight; it was expected to move them (see this manifest's own R6-era _regeneration_note, and task-R7-brief.md's controller amendments) and the divergence from that expectation is recorded here rather than forced. TWO SEPARATE reasons, one per feature: (1) shadows -- none of the three golden_scene_*() fixtures (test_render_raster.cpp) ever populate RenderScene::static_shadow (they hand-build a RenderScene directly, never through scene_from_world(), which is the only place that field gets set) -- render()'s own shadow gate (`options.shadows && scene.static_shadow.has_value()`) is therefore false for all three regardless of RenderOptions::shadows's default, so shade_vertex_color's output is multiplied by exactly 1.0f (sample_shadow never runs) everywhere in all three frames: a mathematical no-op, not merely a visually-small one. (2) the SR-21 overlay-vs-mesh depth bias -- the ticket's own text is specifically about an overlay GROUND-GRID line coinciding with a real TESSELLATED GROUND-PLANE mesh; none of the three fixtures contains a ground/plane-shaped mesh at all (only a box, a sphere, and a cylinder+box), so the exact near-tie the bias exists to resolve never arises in any of them, independent of camera angle -- the bias touches only pixels where that specific coincidence occurs. BOTH claims are backed by dedicated, DIFFERENT regression tests that DO exercise each mechanism directly and were mutation-verified (temporarily forcing the relevant production constant to a no-op value and confirming the test then fails): tests/test_render_shadow.cpp's ShadowStep1/ShadowStep3/ShadowPerspectiveCorrectness suite (shadows, using hand-built scenes that DO populate static_shadow) and test_render_raster.cpp's OverlayDepthBias.GridOverlayIsVisibleOverACoincidentGroundMeshNotHiddenByTheFirstWriterWinsTie (the overlay bias, using a hand-built scene that DOES put a flat ground mesh at the grid's own height) -- see task-R7-report.md for the measured before/after pixel counts. If a FUTURE task adds a ground-bearing golden fixture to this file (task-R7-brief.md's own 'welcome but not required' suggestion), that is the first fixture in this manifest expected to actually move for either reason. R7 FIX ROUND 1 (review IMPORTANT I5): that ground-bearing fixture landed in THIS round, not a future one -- 'shadowed_ground_with_caster' below, a real tessellated ground plane (SR-11's own submesh fallback puts it at material 0, not merely the analytic background) plus a box caster, its shadow baked via build_static_shadow_map() and sampled through render()'s own shadow gate. Verified, not assumed, on BOTH counts: forcing RenderOptions::shadows to false renders a DIFFERENT frame (this golden's own test carries that check permanently, not as a one-time authoring step), while forcing kOverlayDepthBias to 0.0 and re-running does NOT move this hash -- the SAME 'clean win, not a near-tie, at this camera's own framing' outcome Goldens A-C already have, for the identical reason (see this ticket's own text above). This golden is therefore the shadow feature's first byte-exact anchor; the OverlayDepthBias.* regression test remains the SR-21 fix's sole anchor, and this manifest no longer promises a future golden will double as one.
_regeneration_note: R6 (directional/ambient/sky lighting) and R7 (sun shadows) are EXPECTED to change every one of these hashes -- flat per-submesh material colour (this task's own shading model) will no longer be what a shaded-mode pixel shows once lighting lands. A hash changing alongside a matching commit that touches lighting/shadow code is an intentional, reviewed move; a hash changing with no such commit is rot. R6 REGENERATION (this change): every hash moved, and legitimately -- render()'s old flat clear colour is GONE, replaced by a vertical sky gradient (RenderScene::Lighting.sky_zenith/sky_horizon) plus an analytic ground for a scene with a standalone ground plane (none of these three fixtures has one, so their background is pure sky-gradient, not flat); DrawMode::shaded now Gouraud-shades every triangle from its per-vertex world-space normal via Lambert N.L + ambient (ruling SR-18) instead of a flat per-submesh colour, so box_shaded_with_overlays and cylinder_static_dynamic_box_top_down move for that reason too. sphere_wireframe_no_overlays uses DrawMode::wireframe, which stays deliberately UNLIT (raster_cpu.hpp's own header comment) -- its hash still moved, but ONLY because of the background sky gradient, not because its geometry's colour changed. R7 (S7a Task R7, actual outcome): NEITHER of R7's two features moved any of these three hashes -- see this manifest's own _changelog entry above for the verified, two-part reason why. This _regeneration_note's original R6-era prediction ('R7 will legitimately move all three again') is therefore SUPERSEDED, not retracted: it was a reasonable expectation at R6, and R7 checked it directly rather than assuming it, which is what this note now records.
_changelog_vqa_a: Task VQ-A (S7a, rulings SR-33/SR-35 -- fix round for the user's CK-2 verdict 'the rendering is pretty horrible'), REGENERATED, all four hashes moved -- kept SEPARATE from R6's and R7's _changelog/_regeneration_note entries above so a later reader can tell the three regenerations apart by CAUSE, not just by date. TWO independent causes, both real for every one of these four fixtures: (1) render/scene.hpp's sky_gradient_color() became ELEVATION-based instead of a plain fraction of screen row (ruling SR-23) -- every one of these four hand-built RenderScene fixtures uses scene.hpp's own default Lighting{} (sky_zenith (0.28,0.42,0.62) != sky_horizon (0.68,0.74,0.80), a REAL, non-flat gradient) with a camera that is not perfectly axis-aligned to a zero-elevation ray at every pixel, so the background gradient's own per-pixel colour changed even though none of these fixtures' MATERIALS or LIGHTING VALUES changed at all -- confirmed directly: these four goldens hand-build Material{}/scene.lighting (this file's own golden_scene_*() functions), never going through world/builder.hpp's WorldBuilder or scene_from_world(), so Task VQ-A's OTHER change (MaterialDesc/LightingDesc's new defaults) cannot be the cause here -- it never reaches these fixtures. (2) the sky lerp form itself changed from `zenith*(1-t)+horizon*t` to `zenith+(horizon-zenith)*t` (found running this task's own Step 7 re-measure: the old form is not bit-exact when zenith==horizon, which does not apply to these four non-flat fixtures, but the reordered arithmetic still rounds a handful of intermediate-elevation pixels to a different LSB than the old formula did at the same mathematical t) -- both causes are geometry-preserving (no pixel changes from 'covered' to 'sky' or back; verified by this same commit's Step 7 re-run of the R9 AgreementMatrix suite, whose flattened-sky comparison is unaffected by either cause and reports the SAME bands as measurement version 1) and colour-only.
_changelog_f3_cross_platform: REGENERATED 2026-09-17 -- ONE frame moved: cylinder_static_dynamic_box_top_down, d617a2fd6527... -> a4dec5698192... CAUSE, root-caused not guessed: commit 9cff29e2 (the ruled F3 overlay change) made raster_cpu.cpp read `if (item.mesh_index != kNoMesh) continue;` in the body-marker pass, so the marker no longer overdraws a body that has its own geometry. Correct, deliberate, and it changes DRAWN OUTPUT. Goldens were last regenerated at feaeb58a, eight days earlier. THE CONTROL WAS ALREADY IN THE FIXTURES AND NEEDED NO BUILD: exactly two golden scenes populate scene.dynamics. box_shaded_with_overlays has mesh_index == kNoMesh, so its marker still draws and its hash MUST NOT move -- it did not, on either platform. This one has mesh_index == 1, so its marker is suppressed and its hash MUST move. THE ONLY FIXTURE THAT COULD MOVE IS THE ONE THAT DID. CROSS-PLATFORM BIT-IDENTITY VERIFIED BEFORE PROMOTION, WHICH IS WHY THIS SAT UNPROMOTED FOR NINE DAYS: this manifest holds ONE sha per frame, so it asserts the two platforms agree, and a value measured on one of them is half a measurement. MSVC/Windows computed a4dec56981920a8cdafbbeb29943a942b5da4694d5033731d7eec395cca71953 on 2026-09-11; gcc-13/Linux (ubuntu:24.04 container, CI flags verbatim: -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSPADE_BUILD_V1=OFF -DSPADE_VULKAN=ON) computed the SAME 64 characters on 2026-09-17. Compared in FULL, never by prefix. Had they differed, the rule was and remains PROMOTE NOTHING -- two platforms disagreeing is a larger finding than a stale golden.

_changelog_sr17a: SR-17a, the atmospheric term (03-world-and-render.md section 16, amended to ALL GEOMETRY AT RANGE by user ruling 2026-09-17). ADDED, NOT MOVED: the four frames above are unchanged, because the engine default horizon_blend_strength is 0 and horizon_blend() returns the surface colour EXACTLY there -- so they stand as controls proving the degenerate case is bit-exact, rather than being regenerated. Adding a golden is strictly safer than moving four. PROVENANCE: measured 2026-09-18 on TWO platforms independently and compared IN FULL, never by prefix -- Windows/MSVC (msvc-ninja-release) and Linux/gcc-13 (Ubuntu 13.3.0, ubuntu:24.04 CI image, CI flags verbatim) both computed 60e6accc797516ed2c3345f1bc808238919165ba01f1653c38514b1639d40f9a. The manifest holds ONE sha per frame, so it asserts cross-platform bit-identity; a value measured on one platform alone would not have been promoted. THIS ENTRY IS HALF OF A PAIR AND IS MEANINGLESS ALONE: its test renders one scene twice and asserts the two frames DIFFER by more than 1000 bytes BEFORE consulting either hash, then pins both ends -- the off arm against shadowed_ground_with_caster, which predates SR-17a. A golden whose subject is a FEATURE must be falsified by that feature's absence, or it pins that the pipeline ran rather than that the feature applied.
_changelog_rnd5: RND-5 (docs/design/rendering/00-decisions.md), REGENERATED 2026-10-03: four frames moved, and the control did not. CAUSE: render::Lighting{}'s default sun_direction changed from {-0.35, -0.86, -0.37}, which is below the horizon under RND-1, to glm::normalize(LightingDesc{}.sun_direction). The value now comes from LightingDesc, by the expression scene_from_world() uses, so a hand-built scene and a default world share one default sun. These four fixtures hand-build their RenderScene and keep that default, so their lambert surfaces and the shadow map's light direction changed. box_shaded_with_overlays: 318a80cdcbbd390791e543f558ccdd96703b9077a8855eafba9598f580f6a397 -> e2b8fb80f29c54e234f09e5dd918f74d6224ab3cb3afe715937e4a7b16afea1f. cylinder_static_dynamic_box_top_down: a4dec56981920a8cdafbbeb29943a942b5da4694d5033731d7eec395cca71953 -> 20e004c340503c4140c3a5889b6b403226d11c0a07d43cac6acff2348042bba0. shadowed_ground_with_caster: 3a4e4101c45827cb251eb76db247f76fe68c54c6a11d590098c9ebd1d7a0f5ef -> 1acd84782179408542e711114e4cf29ed549c3e1e1010d229cda870de89b6184. shadowed_ground_with_caster_atmospheric: 60e6accc797516ed2c3345f1bc808238919165ba01f1653c38514b1639d40f9a -> c9e0fc7ccdbfc747bd732164e46d45b6776ee9042d8e66f7932b43410193339c.
